newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf finance ministers open tariff talks.
newsitem.headline: Gulf finance ministers open tariff talks.

text.p: Finance ministers from the six Gulf Arab states opened talks in Riyadh on Sunday on the long-overdue unification of their custom tariffs needed to open the door for free trade with other economic blocs, Gulf news agencies said.

The finance ministers from the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would discuss steps taken so far to unify customs, they said. GCC foreign ministers will join them later in the day for an enlarged session.
Differences have been blocking such an agreement almost since the alliance's formation 15 years ago and a political decision is needed to clinch a pact, Arab diplomats say.

GCC and European Union foreign ministers agreed in talks in April to set a deadline of no more than two years to complete a free trade accord between the two trading partners -- an issue under discussion for more than a decade.
Unifying GCC standard tariffs, which vary from four to 12 percent, is among key EU demands for a free trade accord which could open lucrative European markets to cheap petrochemicals from the Gulf.

Arab diplomats said the foreign ministers would discuss GCC ties with Iran and Iraq, the Arab-Israeli conflict and the outcome of Saudi and GCC efforts to convince the emir of Bahrain to attend the next Gulf Arab summit in Qatar on December 7.
Bahrain has threatened to boycott the summit because of a territorial dispute with Qatar.
Saudi Arabia, the dominant power in the political, economic and military group, is trying to find a compromise to ensure full attendance at the summit.
